Harvest Time: 6 to 8 weeks after planting. Subsequent harvests occur every 2 weeks for up to 15 to 20 cuts per year, growers typically renew plantings every 6 months
Yield / Year: Up to 100 t/ha/crop (10 kg/m²; ~1 kg/plant).
Ideal Light Conditions: prefers humid conditions and partial shade or cloudy weather. In full exposed sunlight during intense Brazilian dry spells, plants remain smaller and suffer from heat stress
Ideal Soil Conditions: moist, well-drained, humus-rich (but can tolerate drought due to water storing leaves), slightly acidic to neutral range of 5.5 to 7.5
Pathogens: White rust (Albugo), root-knot nematodes, stem/root rot in waterlogged soils, slugs and caterpillars. Solution: well-drained beds, mulch, avoid standing water.
Layout: Plant beneath a medium-high canopy (such as fruit trees, banana/pliquain systems, or native leguminous trees like Inga species)
Intercrop: collard greens (couve-de-folha)
Trees: Under medium-to-high canopy fruit/timber trees: banana, Inga, açaí, or cupuaçu.

Harvest Time: 60 to 90 days after planting,  ongoing growth if pick only outer, larger leaves near the base while keeping the inner core intact. This allows the rosette to continue producing new leaves.
Yield / Year: 11–20 t/ha/yr fresh leaves (Embrapa); note: 0.036–0.698 g/plant in draft likely dry-weight/unit typo.
Ideal Light Conditions: thrives under partial shading (ranging from 30% to 70%). Full sun stresses the plant, forcing it to flower prematurely.
Ideal Soil Conditions: moist,  well-drained, fertile soil with a pH around 5.5 to 7.5
Pathogens: Leaf spots (Cercospora, Alternaria), root-knot nematodes (Meloidogyne), soft rot in waterlogged soils. Solution: raised beds, good drainage, crop rotation, avoid overhead watering.
Layout: Plant under mid-to-high canopy fruit/timber trees to filter direct sunlight and lower local ambient temperatures.
Intercrop: Chives (Allium schoenoprasum) and true coriander (Coriandrum sativum)
Companion Plants: Cariru (Talinum triangulare), Ariá (Goeppertia allouia), Maniva/Mandioca (Manihot esculenta), Coentro (Coriandrum sativum) or Jambu (Spilanthes oleracea)
Trees: Use mid-to-high canopy or fruit/timber trees: banana, papaya, citrus, or native leguminous trees

Harvest Time: First cut ~30–45 days after planting cuttings/seed; continuous ratoon harvests every 3–4 weeks.
Yield / Year: 15–25 t/ha/yr (fresh leaves)
Ideal Light Conditions: Full sun to light/partial shade; grows upright in drier sun and sprawling/rooting at nodes in wet shade.
Ideal Soil Conditions: Moist to wet loamy soil rich in organic matter; adapts to wide range of soils including neutral to slightly alkaline and periodically wet edges.
Pathogens: Generally hardy; occasional leaf spot (Cercospora), white rust, caterpillars, and aphids. Solution: regular cutting, airflow, avoid stagnant foul water.
Layout: Dense groundcover beds (20 × 20 cm spacing) or moist strips/swales along agroforestry borders.
Intercrop: Jambu, chicória, taro/taioba, banana.
Companion Plants: Sweet potato, Crotalaria, chives, moisture-loving herbs.
Trees: Açaí, banana, Inga, or wet-margin fruit trees.

Harvest Time: 60 days after planting, ongoing growth with frequent harvesting of tips
Yield / Year: 30–70 t/ha/cycle (fresh mass, intensive organic); teammate trial: 30.5–32.4 g/plant (~5–8 t/ha at standard spacing).
Ideal Light Conditions: thrives in partial shade or dappled light rather than scorching, direct midday sun
Ideal Soil Conditions: warm, moist
Pathogens: Drop in air circulation- white rust (Albugo), leaf spots (Cercospora/Alternaria), collar rot (Rhizoctonia), root rot (Pythium). Solution: Prune trees
Layout: Plant jambu and other short-cycle greens in rows between trees like Gliricidia or Inga. Place them along bed edges or in strips next to taller crops like corn or cassava and young trees.
Intercrop: Arugula (Eruca sativa), Cassava (Manihot esculenta)
Companion Plants: Crotalaria (fast-growing green manure or nitrogen fixer)
Trees: Plant beneath taller fruit or timber trees: açaí, cupuaçu, or cocoa

Harvest Time: Tubers ~8–14 months after planting rhizomes, harvested as foliage dies back (short-day triggered). Perennial: leave some rhizomes to regrow.
Yield / Year: 2–15 t/ha/yr tubers (FAO EcoCrop); up to ~260 g tubers/plant in Trinidad trials (~20,800 plants/ha).
Ideal Light Conditions: Partial shade preferred (50% shade gave better tuber partitioning than full sun); tolerates full sun if moisture and nutrients are adequate.
Ideal Soil Conditions: Moist, humus-rich, well-drained, fertile loam; EcoCrop pH 6.0–7.0 (tolerates 5.5–7.5); 1,000–2,000 mm rain/yr with a late-cycle dry spell; 22–31 °C.
Pathogens: Generally pest-resistant; occasional spider mites in dry spells, leaf-eating beetles, tuber rot if waterlogged. Solution: heavy mulch, drainage, shade.
Layout: Plant rhizome pieces ~0.6–0.7 m apart (20,800–27,700 plants/ha) in shaded understory strips under banana or young tree rows. Pre-soaking rhizomes in 48 °C water for 10 min improves sprouting.
Intercrop: Cassava, plantain/banana, coffee (FAO EcoCrop), chicória, jambu.
Companion Plants: Chicória (Eryngium foetidum), Cariru, Taioba (shared moist, filtered-light niche), Inga, Gliricidia, Crotalaria.
Trees: Banana/plantain, Ingá (Inga edulis), Gliricidia, Cupuaçu, or Açaí for light shade.

Harvest Time: First ripe fruit ~3–4.5 months after sowing/transplant (70–130 days), then continuous picking for 2–4+ months; pick when calyx turns yellow-brown (~25–30 days after flowering).
Yield / Year: 4–10 t/ha/cycle fruit (horticultural trials; related P. peruviana yields 3–12 t/ha, Embrapa).
Ideal Light Conditions: Full sun to light dappled shade; fruited well in agroforestry systems (UNESP trial); fruiting drops in heavy shade.
Ideal Soil Conditions: Medium-textured, fertile, well-drained loam (pH 6.0–6.6) with no previous Solanaceae crop. Strongly responds to phosphorus (plants at 8 mg/kg P failed to flower/fruit).
Pathogens: Generally hardy; occasional whiteflies, aphids, fruit borers, Alternaria leaf spot, bacterial wilt (Ralstonia). Solution: rotate away from other Solanaceae, stake plants.
Layout: Stake plants and thin to 2–4 stems; spacing ~1.0 × 0.8–1.5 m in sunny gaps or bed edges of the lower mid-layer.
Intercrop: Short-cycle legumes or greens while young (beans, cowpea, maize, cassava).
Companion Plants: Gliricidia or Crotalaria nearby for nitrogen; marigold/basil. Avoid planting next to other Solanaceae (e.g., Cubiu, tomato) to limit shared soil diseases.
Trees: Light-canopy legume trees (pruned Gliricidia, Ingá), banana, or widely spaced young pioneers (Paricá).

Harvest Time: Tubers mature in ~9–11 mo (280–330 days) from planting
Yield / Year: 15–20 t/ha/yr (tubers)
Ideal Light Conditions: Sun to dappled partial shade (climbs trellises or living tree stakes)
Ideal Soil Conditions: Deep, loose, humus-rich, well-drained mounds; EcoCrop pH 6.0–6.7 (tolerates 5.3–8.0). Avoid compacted wet soil
Pathogens: Anthracnose (Colletotrichum), nematodes, leaf-cutter ants. Solution: clean seed tubers, raised mounds, rotate plots
Layout: 1.0 × 1.0 m on mounds with stakes or living tree trellises
Intercrop: Banana, cassava, maize, taioba, jambu
Trees: Gliricidia, Ingá, Banana, Açaí

Harvest Time: First harvest ~6–8 months from sowing (seedlings transplanted at ~45 days), then continuous production for 1.5–2 years.
Yield / Year: 20–40 t/ha/yr fruit typical (4–10 kg/plant); up to ~14 kg/plant/yr (~100 t/ha) reported as upper potential.
Ideal Light Conditions: Full sun to light partial shade (50% shade used in nursery; tolerates dappled agroforestry light).
Ideal Soil Conditions: Fertile, well-drained, organic-rich clay-loam or sandy-loam (trials add 2 kg compost/hole); adapted to acid Amazonian soils (pH 5.0–6.5).
Pathogens: Root-knot nematodes (Meloidogyne), fruit borer (Neoleucinodes), mites, bacterial wilt (Ralstonia). Solution: high organic matter/compost, crop rotation, clean seedlings.
Layout: Spacing 1.0 × 1.5 m to 1.5 × 2.0 m in sunny gaps of the lower mid-layer, with compost in each planting hole.
Intercrop: Short-cycle greens (jambu, chicória), beans, cassava, banana, or young fruit trees while establishing.
Companion Plants: Gliricidia (biomass suppresses Sclerotium), Crotalaria (nematode suppression), Ingá. Avoid other Solanaceae (Camapu, tomato) nearby.
Trees: Gliricidia and Ingá lopped regularly for mulch; banana, açaí, or cupuaçu in a sparse canopy.

Harvest Time: Sweet varieties: 6–9 mo | Bitter varieties: 12–18 mo (leaves from 50–70 days)
Yield / Year: 5–15 t/ha/yr smallholder avg (up to 30 t/ha/yr improved)
Ideal Light Conditions: Full sun (shade sharply reduces root starch yield)
Ideal Soil Conditions: Light-to-medium, well-drained sandy loam; EcoCrop pH 5.5–8.0 (tolerates 4.0–9.0). Intolerant of waterlogging
Pathogens: Cassava bacterial blight, root rot (Phytophthora), mites, mealybugs, whiteflies. Solution: clean stem cuttings, well-drained mounds, crop rotation
Layout: 1.0 × 1.0 m (early-stage agroforestry intercrop)
Intercrop: Maize, cowpea, beans, banana, young fruit trees
Trees: Young Açaí, Cupuaçu, Pupunha, Paricá (before canopy closes)

Harvest Time: Leaves: ~60–75 days (continuous cuts); Corms/tubers: 180–545 days, early types ~120 days (EcoCrop).
Yield / Year: 6–12 t/ha/yr avg, 25–37 t/ha/yr opt (corms); ongoing leaves
Ideal Light Conditions: Thrives in filtered/partial shade (30–50% shade ideal for tender large leaves); tolerates full sun if soil stays moist.
Ideal Soil Conditions: Loose, fertile, moist, high-organic well-drained loam; EcoCrop pH 5.5–7.0 (tolerates 4.5–7.8). Sensitive to prolonged drought and waterlogging.
Pathogens: Root rot (Pythium/Phytophthora) in poor drainage, Dasheen mosaic virus, aphids, leaf-eating caterpillars. Solution: well-drained beds, clean rhizomes, mulch.
Layout: Plant on raised beds (leirões or camalhões), mounding organic soil 20–30 cm high to keep roots aerobic during torrential rains; 1.0 × 0.8–1.0 m spacing in shaded alleys.
Intercrop: Banana, cassava, maize, beans, jambu, chicória.
Companion Plants: Inga, Gliricidia, Crotalaria, pigeon pea (mulch & nitrogen).
Trees: Ingá (Inga edulis), Gliricidia, Banana (Musa spp.), Açaí, or Cupuaçu.

Scientific Name: Musa spp. (Musa acuminata / Musa x paradisiaca)
Harvest Time: Bunch ~9–15 months after planting, then continuous harvest as ratoons (suckers) follow
Yield / Year: 10–25 t/ha/yr (agroforestry)
Ideal Light Conditions: Full sun to light shade (about 50–70% light). Needs wind shelter
Ideal Soil Conditions: Deep, well-drained, humus-rich, pH 5.5–7, with even rainfall (1,200–2,500 mm)
Pathogens: Fusarium wilt (Foc), black and yellow Sigatoka, Moko (Ralstonia), banana weevil, nematodes. Solution: resistant cultivars, clean planting material, mulch, thin suckers and prune shade for airflow, add windbreaks
Layout: Rows at 3 × 3 m, or 2 rows of banana between tree lines spaced 6–8 m apart
Intercrop: Cassava, beans, pineapple, taro, ginger, turmeric, coffee, cacao
Companion Plants: Inga, Gliricidia, Crotalaria, pigeon pea, Canavalia, sweet potato (ground cover)
Trees: Inga, Erythrina and Gliricidia (lopped for mulch), widely spaced guapuruvu or paricá, açaí, cupuaçu

Harvest Time: Perennial climber propagated by stem cuttings; leaves harvested year-round as needed once established (~6–12 months).
Yield / Year: No standard t/ha commercial benchmark (continuous perennial culinary/medicinal foliage).
Ideal Light Conditions: Partial shade / dappled forest-edge light (propagated under shade cloth); tolerates more sun once roots are shaded and established.
Ideal Soil Conditions: Sandy, sandy-clay, or clay soil rich in organic matter and well-drained; 20–30 °C (Embrapa Rondônia).
Pathogens: Naturally pest- and fungus-repellent (high allyl sulfide/garlic compounds); rarely affected except root rot in stagnant water.
Layout: Semi-climbing shrub (3 m+) requiring trellis or living support at ~2–3 m intervals; best stem cuttings are ~1 cm diameter with ~6 shoots.
Intercrop: Cacao, cupuaçu, banana, and shade-tolerant greens (jambu, chicória).
Companion Plants: Acts as a natural pest-deterring garlic-scented vine; Gliricidia or Ingá provide living support.
Trees: Climbs living support trees or trellises: Gliricidia, Ingá, açaí, cupuaçu, or mid-layer fruit trees.

Harvest Time: First fruit ~3–4 yrs after planting; fruits drop naturally when ripe (~4–5 mo after flowering)
Yield / Year: 5–10 t/ha/yr fruit (mature managed agroforestry)
Ideal Light Conditions: Partial shade (30–50% shade when young; 20–30% dappled canopy at maturity)
Ideal Soil Conditions: Deep, fertile, well-drained acid loam rich in organic matter; EcoCrop pH 5.0–6.5 (tolerates 4.5–8.5). Avoid waterlogging
Pathogens: Witches' broom (Moniliophthora perniciosa), fruit borer (Conotrachelus humeropictus). Solution: resistant Embrapa clones, sanitary pruning, remove fallen mummies
Layout: 5 × 5 m or 6 × 6 m under canopy shade
Intercrop: Banana, açaí, pupunha, cassava, taioba
Trees: Açaí, Pupunha, Ingá, Castanha-do-Pará, Paricá

Harvest Time: First cut ~1 year after planting (allow roots to establish in year 1), then 2–3 cuts/yr (every 3–6 months) at ~50 cm height; woodlots 3–4 years.
Yield / Year: 5–20 t/ha/yr dry matter (Embrapa; EcoCrop 9–16 t/ha dry / up to 43 t/ha fresh; ~4.4–5.8 t/ha in Amazon SAF/alley trials); 8–21 m³/ha/yr wood.
Ideal Light Conditions: Full sun; excess shade reduces growth and biomass.
Ideal Soil Conditions: Drought-resistant and adaptable to low-fertility well-drained soils; EcoCrop pH 5.5–6.2 (tolerates 4.5–8.0). Avoid waterlogging. Fixes nitrogen (leaves ~3% N).
Pathogens: Generally very resilient; occasional aphids, leaf-eating caterpillars, root rot in prolonged saturation. Note: leaves/seeds/bark toxic to horses and humans (safe for cattle/goats).
Layout: Alley hedgerows: 1 m within rows, 3–6 m between rows (0.5 m for dense fodder banks; 1–2 m for intercrops), or 6 × 6 m for shade/living support.
Intercrop: Maize, beans, cassava (less competition than Leucaena), cacao, cupuaçu, coffee, banana, black pepper (living support), pasture.
Companion Plants: Nitrogen-fixing service tree (~3% N leaves): Cubiu (biomass suppresses Sclerotium), Banana, Cupuaçu, Crotalaria, pigeon pea.
Trees: Itself a lopped nitrogen-fixing tree; pairs with Ingá, banana, cupuaçu, cacao, açaí, or coconut.

Harvest Time: First bearing year 2–3 (grafted) or 3–5 (seedlings); fruit ripens ~4–6 months after flowering. Plant at the start of the rains.
Yield / Year: 5–18 t/ha/yr in managed orchards (EcoCrop 7.6–18 t/ha; Cerrado ~6 t/ha; Embrapa Roraima up to 23 t/ha at yr 4); 10–25 fruits/tree/yr (~1 kg each).
Ideal Light Conditions: Full sun for best flowering and fruit set; young trees tolerate partial shade.
Ideal Soil Conditions: Deep, well-drained, fertile sandy-clay or sandy-loam, pH 5.5–6.5 optimal (EcoCrop tolerates 4.5–8.0). Intolerant of waterlogging.
Pathogens: Fruit borer (Cerconota anonella), seed borer (Bephratelloides), anthracnose (Colletotrichum), Phytophthora root rot, mealybugs. Solution: bag young fruits, hand-pollinate, prune for airflow, ensure drainage.
Layout: 5 × 5 m to 6 × 6 m (up to 7 × 7 m in mixed agroforestry); planting pits 40–60 cm with compost. Prune to manageable harvest height.
Intercrop: Banana (early nurse shade), cassava, beans, pineapple, ginger, turmeric, jambu in early years.
Companion Plants: Gliricidia, Ingá, pigeon pea, Crotalaria, Canavalia.
Trees: Ingá and Gliricidia lopped for mulch; banana for early shade; cupuaçu below; widely spaced emergents (>70% light to Graviola crown).

Harvest Time: Leaves from 2–3 months (60–120 days) after planting cuttings, then continuous pruning of young shoots every 60–90 days.
Yield / Year: 15–30 t/ha/yr fresh leaves in dense managed hedgerows with successive cuts (Embrapa CT 156).
Ideal Light Conditions: Best in full sun (heliophyte); tolerates partial shade. Seedlings establish better under 30–50% shade.
Ideal Soil Conditions: Rustic; adapts to most well-drained soils without high fertility (use raised mounds in wet soil); Embrapa pH 5.5–6.0. Drought-tolerant and tolerates light frost (~10 °C min).
Pathogens: Hardy; occasional leaf-cutter ants, scale insects, aphids, root rot in standing water. Embrapa cautions year-round heat + high humidity can stress intensive commercial cuts. Solution: drainage, prune for airflow.
Layout: Leaf production: 1.0–1.3 × 0.4–0.6 m (UFRRJ). Climber on trellis: 1.5 × 2.0 m (Epagri). Thorny—keep away from main footpaths.
Intercrop: Grown as a living hedge or trellis along bed edges with cassava, banana, maize, beans, or aromatic herbs.
Trees: Climbs on trellises, fence posts, or sparse trees like Gliricidia/Ingá; keep from choking young fruit trees.

Harvest Time: First harvest ~2 yrs after planting; peak yield yrs 4–5 (productive up to 12–20 yrs)
Yield / Year: 0.8–1.5 t/ha/yr dry seeds typical (up to 5 t/ha/yr reported)
Ideal Light Conditions: Full sun for maximum flowering and bixin pigment
Ideal Soil Conditions: Well-drained, moderately fertile loam; EcoCrop pH 5.5–7.5 (tolerates 4.5–8.5). Tolerates up to 4 mo dry season
Pathogens: Powdery mildew (Oidium), leaf-cutter ants, pod borers. Solution: open-crown pruning, ant barriers, harvest dry pods promptly
Layout: 4 × 4 m or 5 × 5 m
Intercrop: Cassava, maize, beans, banana, pineapple
Trees: Paricá, Ingá, Açaí, Castanha-do-Pará

Harvest Time: Leaves/tips: 60–90 days after planting (cutting branches 30–50 cm long), then continuous. Calyces: ~4–6 months (128–172 days), picked in staggered harvests (short-day flowering).
Yield / Year: 5–10 t/ha/cycle fresh leaves; 1.5–3 t/ha/cycle fresh calyces (~1.5 kg fresh / 156 g dry calyces/plant with 5 staggered harvests vs ~0.6 kg single harvest, UFLA).
Ideal Light Conditions: Full sun; short-day flowering plant. Needs high light for calyx production and color.
Ideal Soil Conditions: Well-drained, fertile sandy-loam to loam with organic matter; EcoCrop pH 5.5–7.5 (ideal 5.5–6.5, tolerates 4.5–8.5). Sensitive to salty irrigation water and waterlogging.
Pathogens: Foot/stem rot (Phytophthora), powdery mildew, flea beetles, aphids, leaf-cutter ants, root-knot nematodes. Solution: drainage, full sun airflow, rotate with legumes.
Layout: 1.0–1.5 m between plants (Embrapa); cut branches at 30–50 cm for harvest. Plant on sunny edges of beds or open alleys.
Intercrop: Beans, cowpea, maize, cassava, or sweet potato while young.
Companion Plants: Gliricidia, Crotalaria, pigeon pea (nitrogen fixers), sesame, basil.
Trees: Sparse/young overstory only (Gliricidia or Ingá heavily lopped so full light reaches it). Avoid dense shade.

Harvest Time: First fruit harvest ~4–5 yrs after planting; main harvest Jul–Dec (off-season Jan–Jun); palmito from thinned stems
Yield / Year: 6–12 t/ha/yr fruit (managed agroforestry; higher with irrigation)
Ideal Light Conditions: Full sun when mature; young palms thrive under partial shade
Ideal Soil Conditions: Humid, organic-rich, acidic lowland or floodplain soils; EcoCrop pH 5.0–5.5 (tolerates 4.5–6.5). Tolerates seasonal flooding
Pathogens: Anthracnose (Colletotrichum), palm weevil (Rhynchophorus palmarum), aphids. Solution: clump thinning (3–4 stems/clump), airflow, clean sanitation
Layout: 5 × 5 m or 6 × 6 m clumps (managed to 3–4 stems per clump)
Intercrop: Cupuaçu, banana, cassava, cacao, taioba, jambu
Trees: Paricá, Castanha-do-Pará, Ingá, Banana

Harvest Time: Flowers Feb–May, pods ripen several months later (first fruit ~2–3 yrs); pruning for mulch from year 1–2
Yield / Year: 8–15 t/ha/yr dry mulch biomass (pruned alleys); edible pods as secondary harvest
Ideal Light Conditions: Full sun; fast-growing canopy shade tree
Ideal Soil Conditions: Adapts to poor, acidic, well-drained tropical soils; EcoCrop pH 5.0–6.5 (tolerates 4.5–8.0). Fixes nitrogen
Pathogens: Few major pests; occasional caterpillars, scale insects, leaf spot. Solution: regular alley pruning for airflow
Layout: 6 × 6 m to 10 × 10 m (shade/alley rows)
Intercrop: Cupuaçu, cacao, coffee, banana, cariru, taioba
Trees: Paricá, Castanha-do-Pará, Açaí

Harvest Time: Grafted trees fruit from year 3–5 (seedlings 5–8). Fruit ripens 3–6 months after flowering, mainly summer to autumn
Yield / Year: 10–25 t/ha/yr (100–250 fruits/tree/yr, 5–30 kg each)
Ideal Light Conditions: Full sun when mature. Young trees tolerate partial shade
Ideal Soil Conditions: Deep, well-drained loam, pH 5.5–7, with 1,500+ mm rainfall. Moderately drought-tolerant once established
Pathogens: Fruit rot (Rhizopus), stem-end rot (Lasiodiplodia), Phytophthora root and stem rot, Colletotrichum dieback, fruit borer (Diaphania), mealybugs. Solution: drainage, prune for airflow, bag fruit, sanitation, remove mummified fruit
Layout: 10 × 10 to 12 × 12 m. Restrain to ~6 m by pruning for easier harvest
Intercrop: Cacao, coffee, black pepper, pineapple, banana (early years), ginger, turmeric
Companion Plants: Inga, Gliricidia, pigeon pea, Canavalia, Crotalaria
Trees: Inga, açaí, cupuaçu in the lower layers. Avoid close planting with other large canopy trees

Harvest Time: First leaf cut 60–90 days after transplanting, then every 35–45 days. Pods from ~6–8 months
Yield / Year: 10–30 t/ha/yr (fresh leaves); 3–10 t/ha/yr (pods)
Ideal Light Conditions: Full sun. Yield drops under heavy shade
Ideal Soil Conditions: Well-drained sandy loam, pH 6–7.5. Very drought-tolerant, highly intolerant of waterlogging
Pathogens: Pythium/Phytophthora root rot, Cercospora leaf spot, powdery mildew (Oidium), caterpillars, termites, leaf-cutter ants. Solution: raised beds or mounds, no overwatering, prune to ~1–2 m to keep airflow
Layout: Dense hedgerows at 1 × 0.5 m (leaf), or 3 × 3 m (pods). Also good as border or alley-crop rows
Intercrop: Cowpea, beans, sorghum, maize, cassava, okra, sweet potato
Trees: Sparse overstory only (Gliricidia, Inga lopped regularly). Suits the semi-arid Northeast and the Cerrado

Harvest Time: Fruit: ~3–4 yrs after planting (annual bunches) | Palmito: first cut ~18–24 mo, ongoing offshoots
Yield / Year: 5–10 t/ha/yr fruit (agroforestry) or 1.5–2.5 t/ha/yr heart of palm
Ideal Light Conditions: Full sun for fruit/palmito; young palms tolerate light shade
Ideal Soil Conditions: Deep, well-drained, fertile acidic soils; EcoCrop pH 5.0–6.5 (tolerates 4.0–7.5). Intolerant of waterlogging
Pathogens: Palm weevil (Rhynchophorus palmarum), fruit rot, mites. Solution: spineless cultivars, balanced mulch, clean harvest cuts
Layout: 5 × 5 m (fruit) or 2 × 1 m (dense palmito rows)
Intercrop: Cupuaçu, banana, cassava, cacao, black pepper
Trees: Açaí, Castanha-do-Pará, Ingá, Paricá

Harvest Time: Timber ~8–15 years. Leaves and fruit as biopesticide material once mature
Yield / Year: 15–25 m³/ha/yr (timber)
Ideal Light Conditions: Full sun
Ideal Soil Conditions: Tolerant of many soils, pH 5–8, prefers well-drained loam. Drought-tolerant
Pathogens: Few serious pests. Occasional leaf spots, wood borers, root rot in waterlogged soil, leaf-cutter ants. Solution: good drainage, ant control. Note: fruits are toxic to people and livestock
Layout: 5 × 5 m, or lines at 8–10 m for windbreaks or alley systems
Intercrop: Beans, maize and cassava early on. Pasture (silvopasture), with livestock kept from fruit
Trees: Plant beside native trees such as ipê or Mimosa scabrella. Don't plant near forest edges (invasive risk)

Harvest Time: Flowers yr 5–6; bears fruit at 10–20 yrs (fruit ripens ~12 mo; harvest late Nov–early Jun)
Yield / Year: 100–120 kg unshelled nuts/tree/yr at maturity (~2–4 t/ha/yr in mature groves)
Ideal Light Conditions: Full sun at maturity; young trees need partial shade until 5–7 yrs old
Ideal Soil Conditions: Deep, well-drained clay-loam terra firme soils; EcoCrop pH 5.5–7.0 (tolerates 4.5–8.0). High humidity (79–86%)
Pathogens: Leaf blight, seedling damping-off, rodents/agoutis (also natural dispersers). Solution: shade-nurse young trees, keep forest pollinators nearby
Layout: 10 × 10 m to 15 × 15 m (long-term emergent grid)
Intercrop: Cupuaçu, açaí, banana, cassava (early years)
Trees: Açaí, Cupuaçu, Pupunha, Ingá, Paricá

Harvest Time: Timber ~10–15 years. Seeds collected annually
Yield / Year: 20–35 m³/ha/yr (timber)
Ideal Light Conditions: Full sun
Ideal Soil Conditions: Deep, moist, fertile, well-drained soils (Atlantic Forest species). Avoids compaction and waterlogging
Pathogens: Leaf-cutter ants, defoliating caterpillars, stem borers, root rot in poor drainage. Short-lived and brittle in storms. Solution: wind-safe siting, ant control, plant in mixed stands, not monoculture
Layout: 6 × 4 to 8 × 4 m tree lines, or widely spaced shade trees (10–12 m)
Intercrop: Coffee, cacao, yerba mate, banana, palmito juçara
Trees: Ipê, jequitibá, pau-brasil, Inga. Deciduous, so it gives seasonal light

Harvest Time: Timber: first thinning ~4–5 years, final cut ~6–10 years. Seeds: annual
Yield / Year: 15–30 m³/ha/yr (timber)
Ideal Light Conditions: Full sun (shade-intolerant pioneer)
Ideal Soil Conditions: Deep, well-drained clay-loam or latosol, pH 4.5–6, tolerates low fertility. Avoids waterlogging
Pathogens: Leaf-cutter ants, stem borers, Fusarium/Ceratocystis-type dieback, wind breakage of brittle wood. Solution: ant control, wide spacing, no planting in wet, compacted soil, wind-protected sites
Layout: 10 × 4 m or 8 × 4 m tree lines, oriented N–S so crop rows get light
Intercrop: Cacao, cupuaçu, açaí, black pepper, cassava, beans and maize in years 1–2
Trees: Itself the overstory. Mix with Brazil nut, ipê or Inga for diversity
